reply.text:
I'll pull up how your training has actually looked before I say anything. Nothing is logged yet, no sessions, no program and no goals, so we're starting from a clean slate. That makes this the easiest time to set things up so consistency isn't a willpower problem.

Here is what works for most people. Pick fewer days than you think you need, and put them on fixed days. Three sessions you actually hit beat five you plan and miss. Keep each session short enough that a bad day doesn't talk you out of it. Decide when you'll train rather than when you feel like it, and tie it to something already in your week. If you miss a day, the next session is just the next session, with no making up for it.

The simplest first step is a program built around your real schedule. Tell me how many days a week is realistic and about how long you have per session, and I'll set it up. Or if you'd rather start now, I can start a workout.
